messages:
alex: heads-up — p50 on prod model-x jumped from ~18ms to ~45ms after tonight's rollout, observed around 23:12 UTC
maria: saw the same in dashboards, compile queue length spiked at 23:10 :eyes:
kevin: deploy-bot shows the canary rolled at 23:05 — PR #4521 merged earlier today
kevin: looks like the kernel selector heuristics change from that PR might be the culprit
sophie: grabbing perf traces now. can anyone paste the compile logs?
alex: pasting a few lines from runtime-compile.log:
```
[23:09:58] enqueue_compile job_id=2947 model=model-x seq_len=32 kernel_variant=auto_pick_v2
[23:09:58] compile_started job_id=2947 kernel=conv_fused_opt flags=short-seq-weight
[23:09:59] compile_finished job_id=2947 size=2.3MB time_ms=152
[23:10:12] cache_miss key=model-x:kernel:shortseq:9682 -> enqueue_compile job_id=2958
[23:10:12] enqueue_compile job_id=2958 model=model-x seq_len=32 kernel_variant=auto_pick_v1
[23:10:13] compile_started job_id=2958 kernel=conv_generic flags=baseline
```\nkevin: note the different kernel_variant picks within seconds and repeated cache_miss keys — smells like selector oscillation + cache key variance
maria: on the perf side: compile throughput jumped from 0.3/s to 4.8/s for ~3m, p50 latency doubled, token throughput dropped 30%
sophie: kvcache metrics show a lot of fragmentation/evictions at the same time: `kvcache.evictions_per_min = 1200` (baseline ~30)
alex: theory: new heuristic increases short-seq weight but also adds a nondeterministic tie-breaker (timestamp-based salt) — that changes kernel fingerprints and leads to repeated failed cache lookups and recompiles
kevin: i greped the PR and found this line in selector.cc: `fingerprint ^= (now % 97)` — ack. that's the tie-breaker I mentioned
maria: that explains cache churn. we should bisect to before PR #4521 to confirm; can we revert as emergency rollback?
kevin: suggest quick mitigation: revert the salt OR make it stable per-model-version; rollback will be faster while we bisect
sophie: running a local bisect script now: `git bisect start -- HEAD v0.36.9 && git bisect run ./scripts/bench_shortseq.sh`
ci-bot: perf-ci detected regression on branch main: job perf-shortseq showed p50 +120% at 23:14 UTC, blocking merges until triage
deploy-bot: canary flagged: rollout paused at 23:18 due to perf alerts
alex: if we can revert quickly it's safest — rollback request filed on the release channel, cc @oncall
maria: while rollback happens, i'll add a hotfix that removes the timestamp salt and publishes a config toggle to disable nondet tie-breakers
kevin: after hotfix we should run a small repro: 500 concurrent short-seq requests with `./tools/load.py --model model-x --seq 32 --qps 200` and watch compile queue
sophie: btw profilers show compile lock contention on compiler-worker-3: `syscalls blocked waiting for nvrtc` — repeated kernel compiles are saturating the GPU compile service
kevin: good note. repeated NVRTC compilations are expensive; we need dedupe on compile key generation too
alex: agreed. immediate steps: 1) rollback PR #4521 from canary 2) hotfix to remove salt 3) postmortem and automated test for deterministic fingerprints
maria: I'll open rollback PR in 5m and ping release. After rollback, let's watch kvcache.evictions and compile rate for 20m window
sophie: collecting flamegraphs and will upload artifacts to the thread once done
kevin: once stable we should add a CI regression test that runs short-seq microbench with varying seq_len distribution to catch selector oscillations
ci-bot: noted. creating perf regression ticket and assigning to eng-runtime team
alex: thanks everyone — keeping this thread as single source. update here after rollback confirmation :thumbsup:
